_batch: CL Mock Board Exam - Full 200 (Balanced Answer Key)

1.question: The authority to search Vehicles, Other Carriers under Section 222 of CMTA extends to persons, animals when they are suspected of:

choices.A: Holding and Conveying illegal goods
choices.B: Holding or conveying dutiable or prohibited goods
choices.D: Holding or conveying dutiable or forfeitable goods

1.reason: Section 222 of the CMTA provides that the authority to stop, search, and examine extends to vehicles, carriers, persons, or animals suspected of holding or conveying dutiable or prohibited goods.

2.question: Who submits an adequate statement of the facts involved in rulings if the matter is not otherwise appealed for review in ordinary course?

choices.A: Customs Officer

2.reason: Under the CMTA framework, the District Collector submits an adequate statement of the facts involved in rulings when the matter is not otherwise appealed for review in the ordinary course.

3.question: The Commissioner may delegate powers vested upon him under CMTA and this can be delegated to any customs officers with rank of division chief or higher. What may be delegated by the Commissioner?

choices.A: All of the above may not be delegated by the Commissioner
choices.B: Issuance of a Notice of Seizure

3.reason: Under Section 201(e) of the CMTA, the Commissioner may delegate powers to any customs officer with the rank equivalent to division chief or higher. The non-delegable powers are: (1) promulgation of rules and regulations; (2) issuance, revocation or modification of rulings; and (3) compromise or abatement of customs obligations. Issuance of a Notice of Seizure is not among the non-delegable powers.

4.question: The office in the Bureau of Customs which is directly under the OCOM but reports to the Dep. Com. IG for its daily activities, that is responsible for the proper maintenance of the e2m Selectivity Module thru continuous updating of risk parameters.

choices.A: Office of the District Collector

4.reason: The Management Information System and Technology Group (MISTG) is the office directly under the Office of the Commissioner (OCOM) but reports to the Deputy Commissioner for Internal Group (IG) for its daily activities, and is responsible for the proper maintenance of the e2m Selectivity Module through continuous updating of risk parameters.

5.question: Under CMTA, when should the special surveillance of vessels/aircrafts and cargoes on board start?

choices.A: Upon submission of electronic Inward Cargo Manifest (ICM).

5.reason: Under CMTA, special surveillance of vessels/aircrafts and cargoes on board commences upon entry into Philippine territory.

6.question: A Deputation Order was issued by Collector of Customs to Police Captain Mark Balolong for his exercise of police authority. Is this a valid Deputation Order?

choices.A: Yes, because the authority shall be exercised outside of customs premises.
choices.B: No, because the authority is not valid under CMTA.
choices.C: No, because the exercise of power to visit and inspect is exclusive to customs officers.
choices.D: No, because the exercise of police authority is subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.

6.reason: A Deputation Order must be issued by the Commissioner of Customs, not by a Collector of Customs. The authority to deputize law enforcement agencies is vested in the Commissioner under CMTA.

7.question: What is the immediate significance of a vessel loaded with imported goods entering the Philippine territory to discharge laden goods?

choices.A: Vessel will undergo boarding formalities.
choices.B: The goods are automatically deemed abandoned if unclaimed.
choices.D: Duties and taxes will be collected on the imported goods.

7.reason: Importation begins when a vessel carrying imported goods enters the Philippine territory with the intention to discharge laden goods. This triggers customs jurisdiction over the goods.

8.question: Is there a need for a Mission Order (MO) to implement a Letter of Authority (LOA)?

choices.A: A Mission Order must be issued to authorize the implementation of a LOA.
choices.B: A LOA may be implemented without a need for a Mission Order.
choices.C: It depends on the Commissioner of Customs.
choices.D: If LOA is exercised within customs premises, there is no need for a MO.

8.reason: A Letter of Authority (LOA) requires a Mission Order to implement it. The Mission Order provides the specific authority and instructions for the customs officers to carry out the inspection or search.

9.question: What is the Collection District number of Port of Limay?
9.reason: The Port of Limay is under Collection District No. XIV (14).

10.question: The following are sub-ports of Collection District No. XIV, except:

choices.A: Subport of Mariveles

10.reason: The sub-ports of Collection District No. XIV include Subport of Irene, Subport of Currimao, and Laoag International Airport. Mariveles is a sub-port of a different collection district.

11.question: Which of the following shall be considered as Customs duties?

choices.A: Bulk and Break Bulk Discharge Port Survey Fee
choices.C: SCCL Processing Fee of List of Importables

11.reason: The question is flawed as none of the choices are customs duties. Customs duties refer to the taxes imposed on imported goods. All listed are customs service fees, not customs duties.

12.question: Which of the following agencies has the right to access and be furnished with copies of liquidated goods declaration as final liquidation of duties from?

choices.A: All of the above

12.reason: NEDA, Tariff Commission, and PSA all have the right to access and be furnished with copies of liquidated goods declarations as final liquidation of duties.

13.question: When is importation deemed terminated if the imported goods are subject to payment of customs duties and taxes?

choices.A: Upon payment of duties and taxes and legal clearance for withdrawal has been granted.
choices.C: Upon payment of customs duties and taxes and legal permit for withdrawal has been granted.
choices.D: Upon delivery to the consignee's place.

13.reason: Under Papa v. Mago, importation is terminated only upon the payment of duties, taxes and other charges upon the articles, or secured to be paid, at the port of entry and the legal permit for withdrawal shall have been granted.

14.question: What is the prescribed time frame for a beneficiary of an Advance Ruling on Valuation to file for extension of period of the validity of the Advance Ruling?

choices.A: Must be filed at least 90 working days before expiration
choices.B: Application for revalidation must be filed at any time before expiration of the Advance Ruling
choices.C: Must be filed at least 90 calendar days before expiration
choices.D: Must be filed at least 60 days before expiration

14.reason: Under CMTA implementing rules, an application for revalidation or extension of an Advance Ruling must be filed at least sixty (60) days before its expiration.

15.question: How shall the Philippines be divided for administrative purposes and efficient discharge of the functions of the Bureau of Customs bureaucracy?

choices.A: The Philippines shall be divided into as many Customs Districts as necessary.
choices.B: The Philippines shall be divided into as many Ports of Entry as necessary.
choices.C: The Bureau of Customs shall have four (4) and up to six (6) Deputy Commissioners of Customs and each Deputy Commissioner appointed by the President shall have specialized functions.
choices.D: The Philippines shall be made up of different customs territories and separate customs territories.

15.reason: For administrative purposes and efficient discharge of the functions of the Bureau of Customs, the Philippines shall be divided into as many Customs Districts as necessary.

16.question: Is the Collector of Mariveles correct on his contention?

choices.A: Yes, since the Collector of Mariveles has the basis for his collection district objection.
choices.B: Yes, that is valid raising his concern to Secretary of Finance.
choices.C: Yes, since only the Commissioner is empowered to designate such power.
choices.D: No, since the President has the power to appoint.

16.reason: The designation of principal ports and collection districts is a power vested in the Commissioner of Customs, subject to the approval of the Secretary of Finance. The Collector of Mariveles cannot question this designation based on the activity level of his port.

17.question: Who has the authority to open and close Ports of Entry?

choices.A: District Collector

17.reason: The authority to open and close ports of entry is vested in the President of the Philippines.

18.question: Which of the following may not be delegated by the Commissioner of Customs to a subordinate customs officer?

choices.A: Issuance, revocation or modification of rulings.
choices.B: Compromise or abatement of customs obligations.
choices.D: All of the above cannot be delegated by the Commissioner.

18.reason: Under Section 201(e) of the CMTA, the Commissioner cannot delegate the following powers: (1) Promulgation of rules and regulations; (2) Issuance, revocation or modification of rulings; and (3) Compromise or abatement of customs obligations.

19.question: A Customs Personnel Order (CPO) signed by the Commissioner and the Secretary of Finance designating the Deputy Commissioner, AOCG as the full authority to accept applications for Advance Ruling on Valuation, process and approve the same. Is this a valid delegation of power vested upon the Commissioner under CMTA?

choices.A: No, as this is a power vested upon the Commissioner which may not be delegated to a subordinate official.
choices.B: No, as the proper subordinate official should be the Deputy Commissioner, RCMG because decisions and rulings relative to customs are inherent to Legal Service an office under RCMG.
choices.C: Yes, because the Deputy Commissioner, AOCG has the technical competence to process and issue Advance Rulings on Valuation.
choices.D: Yes, because the CPO has the approval of the Secretary of Finance.

19.reason: The issuance, revocation, or modification of rulings (including Advance Rulings on Valuation) is one of the powers that the Commissioner cannot delegate under Section 201(e) of the CMTA.

20.question: An importer is engaged in the importation of cooking utensils, different kitchen wares and kitchen appliances. He received offers from a supplier in Indonesia and would want to be sure that when he imports the goods a preferential tariff shall be applied to the importations. An application for an Advance Ruling on ROO was electronically submitted to the BOC for aluminum dipper, wooden ladle and other kitchen wares to be imported from Indonesia.

choices.A: Date of the Advance Ruling
choices.B: Date of lodgment of goods declaration
choices.C: Period of the request of the Advance Ruling

20.reason: The question is incomplete as it lacks the actual choices. The choices appear to be from a different question.

21.question: Locator "A" operating in Subic Freeport Zone would like to sell a portion of its production out to a company operating in the customs territory. The raw materials of the products of the locator are imported from the United States. For purposes of computing the customs duty due on a transaction to the company operating in the customs territory what value shall be used?

choices.A: Transaction value between "A" and the company operating in the customs territory.
choices.B: Transaction value of the imported raw materials.
choices.C: Since the raw materials have been processed into finished product the transaction value for identical goods shall be used.

21.reason: When goods are withdrawn from a free zone into the customs territory, the customs duty is based on the transaction value between the locator and the buyer in the customs territory at the time of withdrawal.

22.question: The officials of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) conducted a search for the purpose of checking proper handling and packaging of imported wines and cigarettes imported by Asthe Inc. Is the search valid if the letter was only signed by the District Collector and not by the Commissioner?

choices.A: No, as per Section 224 of CMTA.
choices.B: No, because the letter must be signed by the Commissioner of Customs.
choices.C: Yes, if payment of internal tax is involved.

22.reason: Under Section 224 of the CMTA, the authority to conduct searches and inspections must be authorized in writing by the Commissioner of Customs, not merely by the District Collector.

23.question: The Chairman of the Congressional Customs and Tariff Oversight Committee:

choices.A: Chairman, Committee on Ways and Means
choices.C: Chairman, Committee of Ways and Means
choices.D: Joint Senate President and Speaker of the House

23.reason: The Chairman of the Congressional Customs and Tariff Oversight Committee from the House of Representatives is the Chairman of the Committee on Ways and Means.

24.question: The Commissioner of Customs is required to prepare an annual report on the performance of the Bureau of Customs. Which of the following should not be furnished with the report?

choices.A: Congress of the Philippines

24.reason: The Commissioner of Customs is required to submit an annual report on the performance of the Bureau of Customs to the President of the Philippines, Congress, and NEDA. The Tariff Commission is not among those required to be furnished with the report.

25.question: Which government agency regulates the importation of Cellular phones and laptops?

choices.A: Optical Media Board, OMB
choices.B: Movie and Television Review and Classification Board, MTRCB

25.reason: The importation of cellular phones and laptops is regulated by the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) as these are telecommunications devices requiring type approval and other clearances.

26.question: What government agency regulates the importation of Cellphones and laptops?

choices.A: DTI

26.reason: The importation of cellphones and laptops is regulated by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) through its Bureau of Philippine Standards (BPS) for product standards compliance.

27.question: Who has the authority to appoint the member of the Congressional Customs and Tariff Oversight Committee from the House of Representatives?

choices.A: Majority vote of the members of the House of Representatives
choices.B: Chairman of the Committee on Ways and Means
choices.C: Speaker of the House of Representatives

27.reason: The Speaker of the House of Representatives has the authority to appoint the member of the Congressional Customs and Tariff Oversight Committee from the House of Representatives.

28.question: Who has the authority to appoint the member of the Congressional Customs and Tariff Oversight Committee from the House of Representatives?

choices.A: Majority vote of the members of the Senate
choices.B: Speaker of the House of Representatives
choices.D: Chairman of the Committee on Ways and Means

28.reason: The Speaker of the House of Representatives appoints the House members to the Congressional Customs and Tariff Oversight Committee.

29.question: A Bureau official proposes automating the enforcement of customs laws, including jurisdiction over forfeiture cases. How should the Bureau approach this proposal?

choices.A: The Bureau can implement the system, but the firm will have no role in enforcement decisions.
choices.B: The Bureau can approve the automation system, but retain exclusive original jurisdiction over forfeiture cases.
choices.C: The Bureau must decline the proposal, as forfeiture cases must remain entirely within the Bureau's control.
choices.D: The Bureau should fully delegate forfeiture jurisdiction to the technology firm for efficiency.

29.reason: The Bureau of Customs has exclusive original jurisdiction over forfeiture cases. While automation of enforcement systems may be implemented, the Bureau cannot delegate its jurisdiction over forfeiture cases.

30.question: What should be done by the concerned sea ports and airports authorities for the effective enforcement of BOC's functions?

choices.A: Provide proper areas for examination and equipment free of charge as agreed with seaport and airport operators
choices.B: Post sufficient security for the goods stored in the seaport or airport terminals
choices.D: They should recognize that BOC has exclusive jurisdiction over imported goods stored in sea ports and airports

30.reason: Sea ports and airport authorities should recognize BOC's exclusive jurisdiction over imported goods, provide proper areas for examination and equipment, and post sufficient security for goods stored in their terminals.

31.question: Which case pertains to the Bureau of Customs exclusive jurisdiction over seized and forfeited cars and RTC are devoid of any competence to pass upon the validity or regularity of seizure and forfeiture proceedings conducted by the BOC?

choices.A: Papa v. Mago G.R. No. L-27360 22, SCRA 857
choices.B: Asian Terminals Inc. vs. Bautista Ricafort, 505 SCRA 748
choices.D: Emile v. Vinuya G.R. No. L-29043 37 SCRA 381

31.reason: In Enrile v. Vinuya (G.R. No. L-29043), the Supreme Court reiterated the principle of exclusive jurisdiction of the Collector of Customs in seizure and forfeiture proceedings, and that a court of first instance lacks power in such matters.

32.question: Which case pertains to the issue on the ordered release of 25,000 sacks of imported rice to the claimants, not withstanding the pendency of seizure and forfeiture proceedings before the Bureau of Customs?

choices.A: Papa v. Mago

32.reason: In Papa v. Mago, the Supreme Court ruled that the Bureau of Customs has exclusive jurisdiction over imported goods for purposes of enforcing customs laws from the moment the goods are actually in possession and control of said Bureau.

33.question: The Commissioner of Customs wrote a memorandum to the Dep. Commissioner, AOCG to issue the implementing rules and regulations on valuation pursuant to CMTA since the Deputy Commissioner's group is the repository of technical knowledge on valuation. Which of the following is valid statement relating to the memorandum issued:

choices.A: It is a valid memorandum as AOCG has the technical expertise to handle the assigned task.
choices.B: It is not a valid designation without approval of the Secretary of Finance as provided under CMTA.
choices.C: It is not a proper delegation of power vested upon the Commissioner under CMTA.
choices.D: It is a valid memorandum as a delegation of powers under CMTA.

33.reason: The promulgation of rules and regulations is one of the non-delegable powers of the Commissioner under Section 201(e) of the CMTA.

34.question: Under CMTA Sec. 1102, importers and exporters may request an Advance Ruling on Classification to clarify whether their goods qualify for preferential tariff treatment. Which government authority is legally authorized to issue this ruling?

choices.A: Department of Finance

34.reason: Under CMTA Section 1102, the Bureau of Customs is legally authorized to issue Advance Rulings on Rules of Origin (ROO).

35.question: Who has the authority to issue the rules and regulations for the establishment of the system for temporary storage of imports prior to goods declaration in case of abandoned or overstaying goods?

choices.A: Secretary of Finance
choices.B: District Collector for the port that he has jurisdiction.

35.reason: The Commissioner of Customs has the authority to issue rules and regulations for the establishment of a system for temporary storage of imports prior to goods declaration in case of abandoned or overstaying goods.

36.question: An application for an Advance Ruling on origin from a construction company was submitted to BOC for a special design roof, steel window and modular concrete wall to be imported from Malaysia. How shall BOC handle the application?

choices.A: BOC shall issue the Advance Ruling requested by the construction company.
choices.C: BOC shall deny the application and refund the application fee paid.
choices.D: BOC shall request for total amount of P4,500 as application fee.

36.reason: An application for an Advance Ruling must be filed at least ninety (90) days before the importation of the product or item. Since the question does not indicate that this requirement was met, the BOC would deny the application.

37.question: An application for an Advance Ruling on ROO from a construction company was submitted to BOC for a special design roof, steel window and modular concrete wall to be imported from Malaysia. How shall BOC handle the application?

choices.A: BOC shall deny the application.
choices.B: BOC shall issue the Advance Ruling requested by the construction company.
choices.C: BOC shall deny the application and refund the application fee paid.
choices.D: BOC shall request for total amount of P4,500 as application fee.

37.reason: An application for an Advance Ruling must be filed at least ninety (90) days before the importation of the product or item. The application must also cover only one product or item.

38.question: What is the CMTA provision with regard to the time frame by which an applicant to an Advance Ruling shall be notified by the Bureau of Customs on the fact that an Advance Ruling has been issued?

choices.A: The applicant shall be notified by way of publication of the Advance Ruling which shall be done within 15 days from issuance.
choices.B: The notification must be done electronically within 3 working days from issuance of the Advance Ruling.
choices.C: The notification must be done within 1 week from issuance of the Advance Ruling.
choices.D: The notification must be done electronically within 3 calendar days from issuance of the Advance Ruling.

38.reason: Under CMTA implementing rules, the Bureau of Customs shall notify the applicant electronically within three (3) working days from the issuance of the Advance Ruling.

39.question: The Commissioner revoked an Advance Ruling which was issued last June 5, 2025. The date of revocation is June 20, 2025. The beneficiary of the Advance Ruling received the revocation notice last July 3, 2025. The ruling was published last July 4, 2025. What is the effectivity date of the revocation?

choices.A: July 4, 2025

39.reason: A revocation of an Advance Ruling takes effect upon receipt of the revocation notice by the beneficiary, which is July 3, 2025.

40.question: The Commissioner revoked an Advance Ruling which was issued last June 5, 2025. The date of revocation is June 20, 2025. The beneficiary of the Advance Ruling received the revocation notice last July 3, 2025. The ruling was published last July 4, 2025. What is the effectivity date of the modification?

choices.A: July 4, 2025

40.reason: A modification of an Advance Ruling takes effect upon receipt of the modification notice by the beneficiary, which is July 3, 2025.

41.question: Commissioner of Customs modified an Advance Ruling on ROO after ASEAN agreed to amend ATIGA rules to increase the minimum value added to 80%. The President of the Philippines has also issued an Executive Order to that effect. How may the beneficiary appeal the Advance Ruling modification?

choices.A: Appeal to the Secretary of Finance.
choices.B: File a motion for reconsideration before the modified Advance Ruling takes effect.
choices.C: File motion for reconsideration within 15 days from receipt of the modified Advance Ruling.
choices.D: Appeal to Court of Tax Appeal within 30 calendar days.

41.reason: Under CMTA rules, a beneficiary who is aggrieved by a modification of an Advance Ruling may file a motion for reconsideration within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the modified ruling.

42.question: An applicant believes that the Advance Ruling issued by the Commissioner is not correct. How will he protect his interest?

choices.A: Proceed with importation and post sufficient security for the release of the goods.
choices.B: File a mandatory motion for reconsideration within 15 days from receipt of the Advance Ruling.
choices.C: File an appeal with the Secretary of Finance within 30 days from receipt of the Advance Ruling.
choices.D: File an appeal with CTA within 30 days from receipt of the Advance Ruling.

42.reason: Under CMTA rules, an applicant who believes that the Advance Ruling issued is not correct must file a mandatory motion for reconsideration within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the Advance Ruling.

43.question: The Commissioner of Customs invalidate an issued Advance Ruling and as a result a motion for reconsideration was filed. If the Commissioner denies the motion for reconsideration what is the appeal remedy for the aggrieved party?

choices.A: The decision of the Commissioner within 30 days.
choices.C: Appeal to the Secretary of Finance within 30 days.
choices.D: Appeal to the Court of Tax Appeals within 15 days from the receipt of the denial.

43.reason: If the Commissioner denies the motion for reconsideration, the aggrieved party may appeal to the Secretary of Finance within thirty (30) days from receipt of the denial.

44.question: During the 15-day period for the owner of importer goods to present evidence of payment by reason of demand from 'visiting' customs officers, what shall be presumed?

choices.A: All of the above.
choices.B: It shall be presumed that the goods as under constructive customs custody.
choices.C: It shall be presumed that duties and taxes have not been paid on the goods.
choices.D: It shall be presumed that the importation of the goods is contrary to law.

44.reason: During the 15-day period for the owner of imported goods to present evidence of payment by reason of demand from customs officers, it shall be presumed that: (a) the importation is contrary to law; (b) duties and taxes have not been paid; and (c) the goods are under constructive customs custody.

45.question: During the 15-day period for the owner of importer goods to present evidence of payment by reason of demand from 'visiting' customs officers, what shall be presumed?

choices.A: It shall be presumed that the importation of the goods is contrary to law.
choices.B: It shall be presumed that the goods as under constructive customs custody.
choices.C: It shall be presumed that duties and taxes have not been paid on the goods.

45.reason: The same presumptions apply during the 15-day period as explained in the previous answer.

46.question: What is an exception to the 15-day appeal period to the Commissioner of a decision of a District Collector?

choices.A: b and c.
choices.B: Appeal in the case of compulsory acquisition.
choices.C: All appeals to the Commissioner of a decision of a District Collector is 15 days.
choices.D: Appeal in the case of denial of a refund application.

46.reason: The exceptions to the 15-day appeal period to the Commissioner include appeals in cases of compulsory acquisition and denial of a refund application.

47.question: May an appeal be filed even without any supporting documents?

choices.A: Yes, but there will be a simple surcharge for non-compliance with appeal rules.
choices.B: No, because Commissioner would not have any basis to render a decision.
choices.C: Yes, but supporting documents must be submitted within a reasonable period of time.
choices.D: No, because the rules are very specific that supporting documents are required in an appeal.

47.reason: Under CMTA rules, an appeal must be supported by the required documents. The rules are specific that supporting documents are required for an appeal to be valid.

48.question: Atty. "A" an appointed agent of "B" Bangkok, Inc. A company manufacturing and exporting to the Philippines to act as its agent in its application for an Advance Ruling on whether a particular product may be considered originating under ATIGA ROO. "A" submitted electronically an application for Advance Ruling. However, after three (3) weeks, "B" also submitted an application for the same product. What happens to the application of "A"?

choices.A: Bureau of Customs shall consider the application of "A" withdrawn and will refund the application fee paid.
choices.B: Bureau of Customs shall process the application which has complete requirements.
choices.C: Bureau of Customs will continue to process the application being the first application and the application of "B" shall be denied.
choices.D: "A" application automatically replaces the application of B.

48.reason: When an applicant imports the goods subject of an advance ruling application within 30 days from filing, the application is considered withdrawn.

49.question: What is the proper action of the BOC if there is finding on their part that an Advance Ruling issued by TC is adverse to the government?

choices.A: There is no action expected to be done by BOC as the matter shall be automatically reviewed by the Secretary of Finance upon receipt of the Advance Ruling from TC.
choices.B: Elevate the matter to the Secretary of Finance within 15 days.
choices.D: Elevate the matter to the SOF within 5 days.

49.reason: If the Tariff Commission issues an Advance Ruling that is adverse to the government, the matter is automatically reviewed by the Secretary of Finance upon receipt of the Advance Ruling from the Tariff Commission.

50.question: As of now not all CMTA provisions have been covered by implementing rules and regulations. If there is dispute at the District Collector's level involving a CMTA provision and the decision rendered was not appealed to the Commissioner, what is the responsibility of the Collector with regard to the matter?

choices.A: The District Collector should inform the Commissioner of the decision and submit the case facts to OCOM.
choices.B: The District Collector shall enforce the rendered decision.
choices.C: The District Collector shall inform the party adversely affected by the decision that he cannot appeal anymore.
choices.D: The District Collector should inform the Commissioner of the decision and submit the case facts to DEP, OCOM.

50.reason: When a dispute at the District Collector's level involves a CMTA provision and the decision is not appealed to the Commissioner, the District Collector should inform the Commissioner of the decision and submit the case facts to the Deputy Commissioner, OCOM.

51.question: Matters considered as confidential may be released upon request of general public?

choices.A: If request is in the context of a judicial proceedings
choices.B: In all of the above circumstances matters considered as confidential may not be released
choices.C: Upon the discretion of the Commissioner of Customs
choices.D: Upon approval of the Secretary of Finance

51.reason: Matters considered as confidential under customs laws may not be released to the general public under any of the circumstances listed.

52.question: Importation purportedly duty and tax exempt was released from customs custody without the covering Tax Exempt Indorsement issued by DOF as provided for by regulation. May the importation be deemed terminated as the importation has legally left the jurisdiction of the Bureau of Customs?

choices.A: Yes
choices.C: It depends on the type of importation.
choices.D: Yes, as the law provides that in case of duty and tax exempt goods its importation is deemed terminated once it has legally left the jurisdiction of the Bureau of Customs.

52.reason: Importation is deemed terminated only upon payment of duties and taxes and legal clearance for withdrawal has been granted. The absence of a Tax Exempt Indorsement means the importation was not validly terminated.

53.question: An importation purportedly duty and tax exempt was released from customs custody without the covering Tax Exempt Indorsement issued by DOF as provided for by regulation. May the importation be deemed terminated as the importation has legally left the jurisdiction of the Bureau of Customs?

choices.A: It depends on the type of importation.
choices.B: Yes, as the law provides that in case of duty and tax exempt goods its importation is deemed terminated once it has legally left the jurisdiction of the Bureau of Customs.

53.reason: Same as above. The importation cannot be deemed terminated without the required Tax Exempt Indorsement.

54.question: Luxebags Incorporated imported 500 pcs of Class "A" bags bearing the logo "LV" of the famous brand Louis Vuitton. The importation is:

choices.A: Restricted

54.reason: Importation of goods bearing counterfeit logos of famous brands like Louis Vuitton is considered prohibited as it violates intellectual property laws.

55.question: Fuji intends to import reproduction machines that can print colored reproductions. Which of the following agencies should Fuji secure import permits, clearance or licenses?

choices.A: DENR and Office of the President

55.reason: Reproduction machines that can print colored reproductions are regulated by the Optical Media Board (OMB) and the Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB).

56.question: Fuji intends to import reproduction machines that can print colored reproductions. Which of the following agencies should Fuji secure import permits, clearance or licenses?

choices.A: MTRCB and BSP
choices.B: DENR and Office of the President

57.question: Regulatory agency for the importation of previously used machinery and equipment.

choices.A: BPS

57.reason: The importation of previously used machinery and equipment is regulated by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI).

58.question: Regulatory agency for the importation of previously used machinery and equipment.

choices.A: DTI

59.question: Bernon's shipment included firearms and ammunition. The Bureau declared them restricted goods under the law. To which government body must these items be turned over?

choices.A: Armed Forces of the Philippines

59.reason: Firearms and ammunition, being restricted goods, must be turned over to the Armed Forces of the Philippines or the proper regulatory agency.

60.question: Shannel transported contraband goods by land from the pier to a private warehouse. Customs officials intercepted the truck while in route. Was this within their jurisdiction?

choices.A: Yes, but only if the goods are accompanied by an incomplete declaration.
choices.B: No, unless a court warrant for search and seizure is first obtained.
choices.C: Yes, because the Bureau may pursue imported goods subject to seizure during land transport.
choices.D: No, because the jurisdiction of customs ends once the goods leave the port.

60.reason: The Bureau of Customs has jurisdiction over imported goods even during land transport from the pier, as importation is not yet terminated until duties and taxes are paid and legal permit for withdrawal is granted.

61.question: Damaged goods overstayed in port storage and no goods declaration was filed. The Commissioner ordered that the cargo be placed in a facility established for temporary storage of imports. What is the legal basis for this action?

choices.A: The authority of the District Collector to manage all abandoned goods.
choices.B: The Commissioner's authority to establish a system for temporary storage of imported goods.

choices.A: For laboratory testing and analysis

215.reason: The exception for importing narcotics is allowed for laboratory, medicinal, or research purposes when duly authorized by the DDB.

216.question: On what specific date does the legal interest on unpaid duties and taxes on imported goods begin to accrue?

choices.A: From the date the goods declaration was formally lodged.
choices.B: From the date when the amount becomes legally due and demandable.
choices.C: From the date the importer receives the official notice of assessment.
choices.D: From the date the hard copy of the Single Administrative Document (SAD) is submitted to the Formal Entry Division (FED).

216.reason: The legal interest begins to accrue from the date the duties and taxes become due and demandable.

217.question: When is an importation that is exempt from customs duties and taxes considered legally terminated?

choices.A: When the goods declaration has been formally lodged.
choices.B: When the Online Release System (OLRS) has been triggered.
choices.C: When the imported merchandise has physically left the jurisdiction of the Bureau of Customs.
choices.D: When the merchandise is loaded onto a truck for delivery to the consignee.

217.reason: For duty and tax exempt goods, importation is deemed terminated once the goods have legally left the jurisdiction of the Bureau of Customs.

218.question: This is an official statement, prescribed by the Bureau and other government agencies, through which concerned parties indicate the customs procedure to be followed for entering or admitting imported goods, along with the required particulars for customs administration.

choices.A: Entry

218.reason: Goods declaration is the statement prescribed for indicating entry or admission of imported goods.

219.question: What is the applicable customs duty rate for imported goods that are disposed of through a public auction sale?

choices.A: The duty rate prevailing on the date of the public auction.
choices.B: The duty rate prevailing on the date of the auction's publication.
choices.C: The duty rate prevailing at the time the goods were offloaded from the carrying vessel.
choices.D: Any of the above choices may be applicable depending on specific circumstances, such as the date of abandonment.

219.reason: The applicable duty rate for goods disposed by public auction is the rate prevailing when the goods were discharged from the carrying vessel.

220.question: Under the CMTA, who possesses the legal authority to officially designate narcotics or synthetic drugs as being habit-forming?

choices.A: PDEA

220.reason: The Dangerous Drugs Board (DDB) is the authority to declare narcotics or synthetic drugs as habit-forming.

221.question: This customs procedure pertains to goods that are in free circulation, leaving the Philippine territory with the intention of remaining permanently outside its borders.

choices.A: Removal from the free zone

221.reason: Actual exportation is the procedure where goods in free circulation leave the territory permanently.

222.question: Classify the type of importation for counterfeit or infringing goods.

choices.A: Regulated

222.reason: Infringing goods (counterfeit goods) are classified as prohibited importation.

223.question: What is the proper legal term for the act of officially submitting or registering a goods declaration with the Bureau of Customs?

choices.A: Submission of goods declaration

223.reason: Lodgement is the official term for the registration of a goods declaration with the Bureau of Customs.

224.question: Under CMTA, the Bureau of Customs is allowed to release specific information to external parties. Which conditions must be met before such information is provided?

choices.A: The requesting party must be a legitimate third party officially registered with the Bureau of Customs.
choices.B: The requested information is not confidential, is intended strictly for internal use, and is utilized for legitimate purposes.
choices.C: The information exclusively concerns import and export data.
choices.D: All of the above conditions must be met.

224.reason: Information may be provided only if it is not confidential and is for legitimate use by the requesting party.

225.question: This term describes any administrative unit within customs that is authorized and competent to perform any or all of the functions enumerated under customs and tariff laws.

choices.A: Bureau of Customs

225.reason: A customs office is defined as a customs administrative unit authorized to perform customs and tariff functions.

226.question: Upon full settlement of the duties and taxes by the importer, what official documents are furnished by the Bureau of Customs?

choices.A: A Certificate of Clearance shall be issued.
choices.B: An official receipt documenting the payment shall be issued.
choices.C: An order waiving the imposition of legal interest shall be issued.
choices.D: All of the above shall be issued.

226.reason: Upon payment, the Bureau issues a receipt or document evidencing payment of duties and taxes.

227.question: Under the CMTA, who is legally authorized to process a lodged goods declaration at the Bureau of Customs?

choices.A: Freight forwarders

227.reason: Only the declarant and licensed customs brokers are allowed to process lodged goods declarations.

228.question: This term defines the act of bringing goods into the Philippines through a fraudulent, falsified, or erroneous declaration of the goods' nature, kind, quantity, or weight for the sole purpose of evading the payment of prescribed charges, duties, and taxes.

choices.A: Technical smuggling

228.reason: Technical smuggling is the fraudulent declaration of goods to evade duties and taxes.

229.question: This customs procedure involves the transfer of cargo from the importing carrier to the exporting carrier under customs control, executed within a single Customs office that handles both the importation and exportation stages.

choices.A: Through shipment

229.reason: Transshipment is the transfer of goods from one carrier to another within the same customs office.

230.question: Classify dynamite based on its type of importation.

choices.A: Freely importable importation

230.reason: Dynamite and other explosives are classified as restricted importation, requiring permits from regulatory agencies.

231.question: This term refers to the complete fulfillment of all customs and governmental formalities required to allow the admission of goods for domestic consumption, warehousing, transit, transshipment, or exportation.

choices.A: Release

231.reason: Clearance is the completion of all formalities to allow goods to be entered or exported.

232.question: How does the Bureau of Customs treat customs transactions that are processed directly by a party rather than through a designated representative?

choices.A: A direct transaction shall not be subjected to more rigorous requirements or be treated unfavorably compared to transactions processed via a designated third party.
choices.B: An importer processing the transaction directly may be subjected to stricter scrutiny compared to those using third parties, due to the technical expertise possessed by customs brokers.
choices.C: Customs transactions shall not be delegated to third-party entities to prevent prejudice against government collection.

232.reason: The Bureau must not treat direct transactions less favorably than those done through third parties.

233.question: The Bureau of Customs is directed not to impose substantial penalties for errors in goods declarations. Under what conditions is this leniency applicable?

choices.A: The errors are not intentional on the part of the declarant.
choices.B: The errors are inadvertent, and there was no fraudulent intent or gross negligence involved.
choices.C: The errors are deliberate and intentional.
choices.D: All of the above conditions apply.

233.reason: Substantial penalties are not imposed when the errors are inadvertent and without fraudulent intent or gross negligence.

234.question: This legal term refers to the geographic areas within the Philippines where customs laws and tariff regulations are enforceable.

choices.A: Philippine territory

234.reason: Customs territory refers to the areas where customs and tariff laws are enforced.

235.question: This term signifies the act of bringing imported goods into a free zone, either directly or by passing through an intermediate transit area.

choices.A: Importation

235.reason: Admission is the act of bringing imported goods into a free zone.

236.question: For regulated goods where the import permit is obtained after the shipment's arrival, at what point must this permit be forwarded to the Bureau of Customs?

choices.A: At the time of lodging the goods declaration.
choices.B: Prior to the payment of customs duties and taxes.
choices.C: At any point before the goods are officially released from customs control.
choices.D: Prior to the Post Clearance Audit Group (PCAG) executing a post-entry audit.

236.reason: The import permit must be submitted at any time before the release of the goods from customs custody.

237.question: Who has the legal authority to establish the guiding principles and rules regarding the relationship between the Bureau of Customs and third parties?

choices.A: The Commissioner of Customs.
choices.B: The Secretary of Finance, in consultation with the Secretary of Trade and Industry.
choices.C: The Collector of Customs, subject to the approval of the Commissioner of Customs.

237.reason: The Secretary of Finance, upon consultation with the Secretary of Trade and Industry, makes the guidelines for third-party relationships.

238.question: Which party is legally liable for the accuracy of the goods declaration, but has no legal liability for the actual payment of the duties and taxes?

choices.A: The carrying vessel

238.reason: The customs broker is responsible for the accuracy of the declaration, while the importer/declarant is responsible for payment.

239.question: What is the prescribed rate of legal interest on overdue customs duties and taxes?

choices.A: CMTA imposes a 20% annual rate, subject to adjustment by the Monetary Board of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP).

239.reason: The legal interest on unpaid customs duties and taxes is 20% per annum.

240.question: Any party who suffers adverse effect from a decision, act, or omission of the Bureau concerning importation, exportation, or any legal claim has the right to file an appeal. What is the stipulated timeline for filing this appeal?

choices.A: The appeal must be filed within fifteen (15) days of receiving the adverse decision.
choices.B: The appeal must be filed within thirty (30) days of receiving the adverse decision.
choices.C: The appeal must be filed at the earliest possible opportunity.
choices.D: The appeal must be filed within seven (7) days of receiving the adverse decision.

240.reason: The appeal must be made within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the adverse decision.

241.question: The overall administration of the Bureau of Customs is vested in:

choices.A: The Secretary of Finance

241.reason: The Bureau of Customs is headed by the Commissioner of Customs.

242.question: By whom are the Commissioner and Deputy Commissioners of the Bureau of Customs appointed?

choices.A: The Secretary of Finance

242.reason: The President of the Philippines appoints the Commissioner and Deputy Commissioners.

243.question: Under the CMTA, what is the allowed number of Deputy Commissioners to assist the Commissioner?

choices.A: Not less than 2
choices.C: A minimum of 4, but not exceeding 6

243.reason: Under Section 200 of the CMTA, the Commissioner shall be assisted by at least four (4) but not more than six (6) Deputy Commissioners.

244.question: Which one of the following is NOT within the scope of the Bureau of Customs' official functions?

choices.A: Collection of customs revenues.
choices.B: Border control measures to combat smuggling activities.
choices.C: The issuance of general business operating permits.
choices.D: Enforcement of customs laws and tariff regulations.

244.reason: Issuance of business permits is not a function of the BOC; it falls under the DTI or LGUs.

245.question: Which court has the exclusive original jurisdiction over cases involving seizure and forfeiture proceedings under the CMTA?

choices.A: Regional Trial Court

245.reason: The Collector of Customs has exclusive original jurisdiction over seizure and forfeiture cases.

246.question: At what exact point does the Bureau of Customs legally acquire jurisdiction over imported goods?

choices.A: Upon the filing of a court case.
choices.B: Upon the full payment of duties and taxes.
choices.C: The moment the goods come into the physical custody or control of customs authorities.
choices.D: Only upon the issuance of a judicial warrant.

246.reason: Customs acquires jurisdiction over imported goods when they are in the possession or control of customs authorities.

247.question: Which judicial body is vested with exclusive appellate jurisdiction over the decisions rendered by the Commissioner of Customs?

choices.A: Supreme Court

247.reason: The Court of Tax Appeals (CTA) has exclusive appellate jurisdiction over decisions of the Commissioner.

248.question: Which specific power of the Commissioner is strictly non-delegable to any subordinate official?

choices.A: Reviewing the actions of customs officers.
choices.B: Promulgating, issuing, or altering customs rules and regulations.
choices.C: The general exercise of granted customs powers.
choices.D: The assignment or reassignment of customs officers.

248.reason: Under Section 201(e), the promulgation of rules and regulations is a non-delegable power of the Commissioner.

249.question: The Commissioner is required to submit an annual performance report. By what date must this report be filed?

choices.A: December 31

249.reason: The annual report shall be submitted on or before March 31 of the following year.

250.question: Which particular type of customs issuance outlines broad policy statements and the detailed implementing regulations of the CMTA?

choices.A: Customs Memorandum Circular (CMC)

250.reason: Customs Administrative Orders (CAO) contain the policy statements and implementing rules and regulations of the CMTA.
